name: Icecream (IceCC)
listed_description: Fork of distcc that distributes C and C++ compilation across hosts, with a scheduler that uses only idle cycles and supports custom toolchains.
claim_text: Distributes builds across hosts via a scheduler using only idle cycles; no numbers given.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 7, Getting the most out of compilers > Reducing build times > Leveraging tools

name: Ninja
listed_description: Build generator backend created specifically to reduce build times; recommended as a faster replacement for the default Make generator in CMake.
claim_text: Ninja is a great one to start with, as it was created specifically to reduce build times; no numbers given.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 7, Getting the most out of compilers > Reducing build times > Leveraging tools

name: sccache
listed_description: Named in passing as a compiler cache alternative to ccache and clcache for Windows builds.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 7, Getting the most out of compilers > Reducing build times > Leveraging tools

name: distcc
listed_description: Distributed C/C++ compilation tool; the book mentions it only as the project Icecream was forked from.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 7, Getting the most out of compilers > Reducing build times > Leveraging tools

name: clcache
listed_description: MSVC compiler cache suggested on Windows in place of ccache; the upstream repo is archived.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 7, Getting the most out of compilers > Reducing build times > Leveraging tools

name: GNU gold linker
listed_description: Alternative linker (with LLVM's LLD) that the book says can help a lot with link time because it supports multi-threaded linking.
claim_text: A different linker such as LLD or Gold can help a lot, especially since they allow multi-threaded linking; no numbers.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 7, Getting the most out of compilers > Reducing build times > Leveraging tools

name: C++20 modules instead of header inclusion (Alibaba Hologres case)
listed_description: Replacing header inclusion with C++20 modules; the book cites an Alibaba blog reporting a build-time reduction on the Hologres data warehouse project.
claim_text: Alibaba reports modules over traditional headers cut Hologres compilation time by 42%.
book_benchmark: Third-party blog figure cited by the book; workload is the Hologres project build, compiler and flags not stated in the book. Blog code not in repo.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 7, Getting the most out of compilers > Reducing build times > Leveraging tools; also Further reading

name: Unity builds and precompiled headers via CMake 3.16
listed_description: Single-translation-unit unity builds (UNITY_BUILD) and target_precompile_headers to cut compile time; the book gives caveats about symbol clashes and memory.
claim_text: Unity builds may speed up projects with plenty of code in headers; precompiled headers speed up subsequent compilations. No numbers.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 7, Getting the most out of compilers > Reducing build times > Leveraging tools

name: Rule of Chiel (compile-time cost of template constructs) and alias-based conditional_t
listed_description: Ranking of template operations by compile-time cost from benchmarking by Chiel Douwes; the book shows an alias-based conditional that compiles faster than the struct-specialization version.
claim_text: The alias-based conditional is faster to compile than the struct-based traditional one, because it avoids instantiating new specializations.
book_benchmark: No numbers in the book; refers to charts in Odin Holmes' CppNow 2017 talk on type-based template metaprogramming.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 7, Getting the most out of compilers > Reducing build times > Rethinking templates

name: Static CRTP dispatch versus virtual calls (Bendersky benchmark)
listed_description: The book recommends CRTP static polymorphism on hot paths and points to Eli Bendersky's article for a concrete measured gap against virtual dispatch.
claim_text: Dynamic dispatch has overhead versus static method calls; the book cites Bendersky's benchmark for the size of the difference, no numbers quoted.
book_benchmark: Book quotes no figures; numbers are in the cited 2013 blog article (virtual call loop versus CRTP loop). Companion repo Chapter06 holds CRTP code but no benchmark.
guessed_category: none: static versus dynamic dispatch idiom
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 6, Applying the curiously recurring template pattern > Knowing when to use dynamic versus static polymorphism; also Further reading

name: std::pmr monotonic and pool resources, with winking out
listed_description: C++17 polymorphic allocators: monotonic_buffer_resource, unsynchronized and synchronized pool resources chained over a stack buffer, plus winking out objects without calling destructors.
claim_text: Pool resources should give much better performance than the global allocator, especially over a monotonic buffer upstream; no numbers.
found_in: book: Software Architecture with C++, 2nd ed. (2025), ch. 6, Dealing with memory efficiently > Leveraging polymorphic allocators
